L63: ##### ARTICLE 1. Scope of Regulation [10130 - 10149]
L64: 
L65:   ( Article 1 added by Stats. 1943, Ch. 127. )
L66: ###### 10131.
L67: 
L68: A real estate broker within the meaning of this part is a person who, for a compensation or in expectation of a compensation, regardless of the form or time of payment, does or negotiates to do one or more of the following acts for another or others:
L69: 
L70: (a) Sells or offers to sell, buys or offers to buy, solicits prospective sellers or buyers of, solicits or obtains listings of, or negotiates the purchase, sale, or exchange of real property or a business opportunity.
L71: (b) Leases or rents or offers to lease or rent, or places for rent, or solicits listings of places for rent, or solicits for prospective tenants, or negotiates the sale, purchase, or exchanges of leases on real property, or on a business opportunity, or collects rents from real property, or improvements thereon, or from business opportunities.
L72: (c) Assists or offers to assist in filing an application for the purchase or lease of, or in locating or entering upon, lands owned by the state or federal government.
L73: 
L74: (d) Solicits borrowers or lenders for or negotiates loans or collects payments or performs services for borrowers or lenders or note owners in connection with loans secured directly or collaterally by liens on real property or on a business opportunity.
L75: (e) Sells or offers to sell, buys or offers to buy, or exchanges or offers to exchange a real property sales contract, or a promissory note secured directly or collaterally by a lien on real property or on a business opportunity, and performs services for the holders thereof.

L77: (Amended by Stats. 2018, Ch. 285, Sec. 27. (AB 2884) Effective January 1, 2019.)

L1@P0: CHAPTER TWO
L2@P0: APPROVAL OF MANAGEMENT AGENTS
L3@P0: 2.1 INTRODUCTION
L4@P0: This chapter discusses the approval procedures for the selection of management
L5@P0: agents. Under different circumstances, HUD, Administration for Rural Housing and
L6@P0: Economic Development Services (ARHEDS), or a state/local agency may be
L7@P0: responsible for approving the management agent. The first section of this chapter
L8@P0: describes four management agent types and lists the conditions under which each
L9@P0: federal or state/local agency has approval authority. The second section discusses
L10@P0: the procedures for management agent approval under HUD authority. The third
L11@P0: section discusses the procedures for management agent approval under ARHEDS and
L12@P0: state/local agency authority.
L13@P0: SECTION 1: BACKGROUND
L14@P0: 2.2 AGENT SELECTION AND APPROVAL AUTHORITY
L15@P0: The project owner is responsible for seeking out and selecting a management agent,
L16@P0: but the selection is subject to the approval of the authorizing agency. This authorizing
L17@P0: agency may be HUD, or it may be ARHEDS or the state/local agency, depending upon
L18@P0: the project type and the mortgage insurance coverage. See Figure 2-1.

L34@P1: Four Types of Management Agents
L35@P1: 1. Owner/Manager
L36@P1: 2. Identity of Interest Management Agent
L37@P1: 3. Independent Fee Agent
L38@P1: 4. Project Administrator
L39@P1: (In this handbook, the term "management agent" applies to all
L40@P1: four forms of management agents unless a specific distinction
L41@P1: is made because of policy or procedural differences.)
L42@P1: 4381.5 REV-2
L43@P1: a. HUD Approval Authority. HUD has approval authority for all multifamily HUDinsured and HUD-assisted projects where HUD is .the contract administrator.
L44@P1: Furthermore, regardless of approving agency, HUD will conduct all Previous
L45@P1: Participation Clearance (Form HUD-2530) reviews for all types of projects.
L46@P1: b. State/local housing agency Approval Authority. State/local agencies have
L47@P1: approval authority for all non-HUD insured projects where the agency financed
L48@P1: the project or serves as the subsidy contract administrator. As part of the
L49@P1: approval process, the state/local agency must submit to HUD a Previous
L50@P1: Participation Certification (Form HUD-2530) for the proposed management
L51@P1: agent as described in paragraph 2-9a. With respect to all other procedures
L52@P1: discussed in this chapter, state and local agencies may develop their own
L53@P1: criteria or elect to use the procedures established in this Chapter. See Section
L54@P1: 3 of this chapter for additional guidance.
L55@P1: c. ARHEDS Approval Authority. ARHEDS has approval authority for all ARHEDS
L56@P1: 515/8 projects. The ARHEDS Office must submit a Previous Participation
L57@P1: Certification for the proposed management agent for all ARHEDS 515/8
L58@P1: projects as described in paragraph 2-9a. With respect to all other procedures
L59@P1: discussed in this chapter, ARHEDS may develop its own criteria or elect to use
L60@P1: the procedures established in this Chapter. See Section 3 of this chapter for

L62@P1: 2.3 TYPES OF MANAGEMENT AGENTS
L63@P1-2: 12/94 2-2 4381.5 REV-2
L64@P2: a. Owner/manager. In this relationship, the owner and the management agent are
L65@P2: the same business entity. This is also referred to as self-management. A
L66@P2: project is not self-managed if some or all of the same individuals are involved
L67@P2: in both the ownership entity and the management agent but the organizations
L68@P2: are legally different business entities.
L69@P2: For example, if the owner is a limited partnership, and the general partner of
L70@P2: the ownership entity serves as the management agent, the management agent
L71@P2: is not an owner/manager because the management agent and the mortgagor
L72@P2: are different business entities. Instead, the management agent is an identityof-interest management agent (see paragraph 2.3b).
L73@P2: b. Identity-of-interest (1011 management agent. An 101 relationship exists when an
L74@P2: individual or entity that provides management services to the project has a
L75@P2: relationship with the project owner that is such that selection of the
L76@P2: management agent and determination of the management fee will not be
L77@P2: determined through an arms-length transaction.
L78@P2: (1) An identity-of-interest relationship exists when:
L79@P2: (a) The owner entity or a general partner of the owner entity, or
L80@P2: (b) Any officer or director of the owner entity, or
L81@P2: (c) Any person who directly or indirectly controls 10 percent or more
L82@P2: of the voting rights, or owns 10 percent or more of the owner
L83@P2: entity
L84@P2: is also
L85@P2: (d) An owner, general partner, officer, or director of the management
L86@P2: agent company or its subcontractor, or
L87@P2: (e) A person who directly or indirectly controls 10 percent or more
L88@P2: of the voting rights, or owns 10 percent or more of the
L89@P2: management company or its subcontractor.
L90@P2: (2) "Person," as used above, refers to any individual, partnership,
L91@P2: corporation, or other business entity. Any ownership, control, or
L92@P2: interest held or possessed by a person's spouse, parent, child,
L93@P2: grandchild, or sibling or other relation by blood or marriage is attributed
L94@P2: to that person for this determination.
L95@P2: (3) "Subcontractor," as used above, refers to any individual or company
L96@P2: that contracts with the management agent to provide management
L97@P2: services to the project.
L98@P2-3: 2-3 12/94 4381.5 REV-2
L99@P3: c. Independent fee management agent. A management company or individual
L100@P3: that has no identity-of-interest relationship with the owner (see paragraph 2.3b)
L101@P3: and no financial interest or involvement in the project, other than earning a fee
L102@P3: for providing management services.
L103@P3: d. Project administrator. An individual who directs the day-to-day activities of a
L104@P3: project designed for elderly, handicapped, or disabled residents, and who
L105@P3: reports to the Board of Directors. Generally, a project administrator is an
L106@P3: employee of the project, rather than a contractor; has a job description and/or
L107@P3: employment agreement with the project instead of a management agreement;
L108@P3: and receives a salary rather than a management fee.
L109@P3: 2.4 PRINCIPLES OF THE REVIEW PROCESS
L110@P3: a. Approval will not be unreasonably withheld. A management agent's contract is
L111@P3: with the project owner. HUD will not unreasonably withhold approval of the
L112@P3: proposed agent for a project.
L113@P3: b. HUD reviews protect the public interest. HUD reviews management agent
L114@P3: performance, experience, and capabilities to protect the public and its own
L115@P3: interests. HUD does not disapprove agents to penalize program participants
L116@P3: who have had past performance problems.
L117@P3: c. Past Performance and Current Bcoerfise are Considered. Loan/Asset
L118@P3: Management staff must consider both the agent's past performance and the
L119@P3: probability of future compliance.
L120@P3: (1) Area Offices will not issue disapprovais based on past performance
L121@P3: without considering corrective actions taken by the agent to address

#### Historical and Revision Notes

#### legislative statements

Section 347(a) of the House amendment adopts a comparable provision contained in the Senate amendment instructing the trustee to stop payment on any check remaining unpaid more than 90 days after the final distribution in a case under Chapter 7 or 13. Technical changes are made in section 347(b) to cover distributions in a railroad reorganization.

#### senate report no. 95–989

Section 347 is derived from Bankruptcy Act §66 [section 106 of former title 11]. Subsection (a) requires the trustee to stop payment on any distribution check that is unpaid 90 days after the final distribution in a case under chapter 7 or 13. The unclaimed funds, and any other property of the estate are paid into the court and disposed of under chapter 129 [§2041 et seq.] of title 28, which requires the clerk of court to hold the funds for their owner for 5 years, after which they escheat to the Treasury.

Subsection (b) specifies that any property remaining unclaimed at the expiration of the time allowed in a chapter 9 or 11 case for presentation (exchange) of securities or the performance of any other act as a condition to participation in the plan reverts to the debtor or the entity acquiring the assets of the debtor under the plan. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
